Glossary

Source: vignettes/articles/glossary.Rmd
glossary.Rmd

Analysis terms

  • NIS: The HCUP National Inpatient Sample, called the Nationwide Inpatient Sample before its 2012 redesign. It samples inpatient stays and is not a census of all hospitalizations.
  • Discharge: One hospital stay represented by a record. A person may have multiple stays; the NIS does not provide longitudinal patient linkage.
  • Data year: The calendar year of discharges in an annual NIS release. It is different from the release date.
  • Release revision: A corrected or distributed version of a data-year release. The data year alone may not identify which file revision was used.
  • Component: A discharge-level or hospital-level file in an NIS release, such as Core or Hospital. easyNIS’s opening and analysis workflows target compatible discharge-level data.
  • Cohort: The discharges meeting a study’s inclusion definition.
  • Analytic domain: A subpopulation for which a survey estimate is calculated while accounting for the original sample design. It is not an independently sampled subgroup.
  • Discharge weight (DISCWT): The NIS weight used to estimate national discharge totals and other weighted quantities.
  • Trend weight: An HCUP weight supplied for specified historical NIS years to improve comparability with the redesigned sample. It is not universal across historical years, and easyNIS does not select it automatically.
  • Estimand: The explicitly defined quantity a study aims to estimate, such as an annual national total or a proportion across several years.
  • Stratum (NIS_STRATUM): A sampling-design group used with hospitals and weights for variance estimation.
  • PSU / hospital (HOSP_NIS): The primary sampling unit in the NIS design. Hospital numbers are year-specific, so easyNIS scopes them by year.
  • Annualization: The nis_design() option that divides weights by the count of valid years included. It treats partial years as full years.
  • Reweighting: Multiplication of design weights by additional analyst weights. In easyNIS this is experimental and changes the interpretation of weighted totals.

Coding and reporting terms

  • Prefix flag: A logical indicator that checks whether an ICD code begins with an analyst-supplied string in one of the selected code slots.
  • CCSR: Clinical Classifications Software Refined, a category system for ICD-10-CM/PCS codes. easyNIS can read a reference file supplied by the user.
  • Primary suppression: Masking a cell that violates a reporting rule.
  • Complementary suppression: Masking an additional cell so a primary suppressed value cannot be recovered from totals. easyNIS’s data-frame helper supports a single-dimension case; it is not a general suppression solver.
  • CCR (CCR_NIS): Cost-to-charge ratio used to estimate cost from hospital charges.
  • Charge: The amount billed for a stay. It differs from the resources used to provide care and from payment received.
  • Cost estimate: An estimate of resources used for care, potentially calculated from charges and a cost-to-charge ratio. Interpretation depends on the method and year.
  • CPI-U: Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers, used by nis_cost() to express amounts in a selected reference-year dollar.
  • Synthetic fixture: Invented data made by nis_example() to demonstrate package behavior. It contains no real NIS discharges.
  • Coding era: The code system applicable to a discharge. In 2015, NIS includes both ICD-9-CM and ICD-10-CM/PCS discharges.

Common pitfalls

Common pitfalls

  • A weight, code flag, or suppression label is meaningful only with its method and assumptions documented.
  • Synthetic fixture outputs are not estimates of the NIS population.
